Storm & Emergency Response for Auburn Township — Since 1982

Auburn Township is Roubic's home — 44 years of family ownership run from the same Taylor May Road yard. When a storm rolls through, the emergency line answers 24/7 and crews roll straight out of HQ, which is why emergency response here is the fastest anywhere in the service area.

The rural context matters. Auburn sits in NE Ohio's high-wind and derecho exposure corridor, and its heritage oaks, mature maples, and EAB-weakened ash are the trees that fail under wind load. Roubic stages chippers, cranes, and sectional-dismantling crews ahead of forecasted high-wind events so multiple Auburn jobs can be worked in priority order.

Emergency Response, Straight From HQ

Because the Auburn Township yard is Roubic's home base, there is effectively no travel time to reach an Auburn emergency — the target on-site window for active emergencies is 2–4 hours, the fastest anywhere Roubic works. Active emergencies mean trees on structures, driveway-blocking falls that cut off emergency-vehicle access, and leaning hazard trees that could fail in the next gust.

Common Auburn Township Storm Questions

Auburn Township Storm & Emergency FAQ

Six things Auburn Township homeowners want to know before a storm hits.

How fast does Roubic respond to tree emergencies in Auburn Township?
Auburn Township is Roubic's HQ, so response here is the fastest in the service area — the target on-site window for active emergencies is 2–4 hours, dispatched straight from the Auburn yard. Active emergencies are tree-on-structure, driveway-blocking, or leaning hazard trees that could fail before scheduled service. 24/7 emergency line: {{global.phone}}.
What does Roubic do for insurance claims on storm-damaged trees?
We provide the full documentation package your carrier needs: scene photos, itemized scope, species and DBH estimates, before/after photos, and a written job summary matched to the carrier's loss notice. Insurance typically covers tree work only when a tree damages a covered structure (house, garage, fence, vehicle), not routine standing-tree removal. Most insurance-coverable jobs land between $1,200 and $8,000.
Will Roubic dispatch during an active high-wind event or storm?
Crew safety governs deployment. We do not send climbers or crane operators up during active high-wind conditions or lightning. Once conditions are safe — typically within 2–4 hours of the storm passing — we deploy aggressively, staging multiple jobs in priority order. For pre-storm preparation, see our Storm Preparation Checklist.
Does Roubic do after-hours work for landscape and property-management firms?
Yes. Several Auburn Township-area landscape and property-management companies use Roubic as their after-hours emergency tree subcontractor. We stage chippers, cranes, and sectional-dismantling crews ahead of forecasted high-wind events so we can compress response time across multiple jobs.
What if a tree falls on my house in Auburn Township after-hours?
Call {{global.phone}} immediately. We'll dispatch a crew with crane support for tree-on-structure extraction, photograph the scene for insurance documentation, tarp the roof opening if needed, and coordinate next-day full extraction and cleanup. Don't enter the damaged area until the crew arrives — branch shifts can be unpredictable.
How much does storm and emergency tree work cost in Auburn Township?
Final price depends on access, height, structure proximity, and equipment. Real Roubic brackets: small trees under 30 ft $500–$1,500; medium 30–60 ft $1,500–$5,000; large 60–80 ft $2,500–$8,000+; X-large or crane-assisted 80 ft+ $2,500–$8,000+. After-hours emergency dispatch adds roughly 30%, and every estimate is free on-site.
